heading: INT. GREENHOUSE ABOVE A CLOSED TRAIN STATION - LATE AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. GREENHOUSE ABOVE A CLOSED TRAIN STATION - LATE AFTERNOON
The glass roof has been mended in panes of different greens.
Tomato vines climb strings tied to old signal wires.
Down below, a freight train sighs through where no passenger train has stopped in years.
The floor trembles gently.
IMELDA CORREIA (70s, small, hands like roots) kneels in the dirt, tying a vine.
Her daughter-in-law, NOOR HASSAN (40s, good coat, car keys held too long) stands at the doorway and does not step in.
Shoes.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: Noor looks at her shoes, clean leather, and takes them off.
Sets them side by side on the threshold.
Walks in on stocking feet.
It's warm in here.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: It is a greenhouse.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: Noor touches a leaf.
Rubs it between finger and thumb.
Smells it.
Imelda watches her without turning her head.
Teo says you haven't been answering.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: The telephone is in the kitchen. I am not in the kitchen.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: He's worried.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: He is busy.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: Noor smiles at that, thin and brief.

At the far end of the greenhouse, a boy of about twelve, TEODORO "TEO" CORREIA-HASSAN (12, serious, glasses taped at the hinge), sits cross-legged between two rows of lettuce, sorting seed packets by colour and not looking up.
He came with me.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: I saw him.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: He wouldn't come over.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: He is where he is supposed to be.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: A long silence.
The freight train hushes the room, then passes.
Noor lowers herself onto an overturned bucket.
Marcos called.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: Imelda ties a knot.
Pulls it tight.
Snips the string with her teeth.
How is the weather in Lisbon?
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: He didn't say.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: Then he did not call for long.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: He called for four minutes. He asked about the house.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: The house is standing.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: He asked whether you were thinking of selling.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: Imelda reaches for a tomato, turns it in her palm, and lets it go.
She picks another.
Presses it.
Hard.
Green.
She leaves it.
It is a little early for these.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: Imelda.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: Three more weeks. I will make the sauce for the church supper. Father Anselmo likes it with basil. I told him I would bring basil.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: You don't have to answer me.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: No.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: She gets up slowly, one hand on her knee.
Crosses the greenhouse.
Takes a clay pot from a shelf and carries it back to Noor, who takes it without being asked.
A basil plant, small and fierce.
Put that in your window. It does not like the dark.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: Noor holds the pot in both hands like something warm.
There isn't much window in the apartment.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: Then it will grow toward what there is.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: Across the glass, Teo has lined up all the packets in a spectrum.
He pushes his glasses up with one knuckle and looks at the two women for the first time.
Then back to his seeds.
The door rattles.
FATHER ANSELMO (60s, round, cassock under a windbreaker) leans in with a bag of potting soil on his shoulder, and behind him GRETA VOLKOV (50s, neighbour, gardening gloves, loud scarf).
Imelda, the basil?
units.name: FATHER ANSELMO

units.text: On the shelf. Shoes.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: We already took them off. Hello, Noor.
units.name: GRETA

units.text: Noor nods.
Father Anselmo sets down the soil and goes straight to the shelf, humming.
I should go. He has school tomorrow.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: He has school tomorrow.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: Neither moves.
Wait.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: She goes to the end of a row and snaps off a tomato vine with two small green fruits on it.
Wraps the stem in a wet paper towel.
Holds it out.
For his windowsill. Not for eating.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: Noor takes it.
Their fingers touch.
Neither pulls back at once.
Thank you.
units.name: NOOR

units.text: Take your shoes.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: Noor goes to the threshold, steps into her shoes, and turns once to look at the rows of green.
Then she crosses to Teo and crouches beside him.
He holds out one packet, wordless.
She reads the label, nods, tucks it in her coat.
Imelda has already turned back to the vines.
She hums something under her breath, badly, and ties another knot.
The next freight train begins to build, far off, in the rails.
